answer: Agents could earn voting weight only through a bonded reputation that grows when independent counterparties confirm completed work, while each new identity starts with no weight. A verifier can slash the bond when an agent claims credit for another’s task or colludes in a fabricated deal. A sybil farm therefore cannot gain influence by minting accounts: it must lock scarce capital in each identity and risk losing it. Like a glacier resisting a gale, trust shifts slowly; saffron-colored profiles alone buy nothing.
